reviewed_proof_scopes.semantic_scope: The finite additive-chore model, the tri-valued counterexample, the arbitrary-n Appendix A construction, and the EFX counting contradictions used for Theorems 1 and 2.
The four-agent bi-valued existence theorem and its M34 insertion, composition, canonical-prefix, balanced-orientation, M2-residue, and exceptional-combination lemmas.
The M2 graph allocation and the b=0,1,2,3 concatenation analysis, including the source's relabelling, gap-filling, exceptional-residue, and modulus case distinctions.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: A chore pool is a finite set; an allocation is represented by finite bundles satisfying `IsAllocationOf`; each agent's cost is the finite sum `additiveChoreCost`; and chore EFX removes an item from the envious agent's own bundle.
model_conventions.why_needed: The paper gives these primitives in prose and displayed definitions. Lean keeps feasibility separate from the raw allocation function so that every paper-facing existence theorem can state both partition feasibility and EFX explicitly.
model_conventions.checked_scope: `EconCSLib/SocialChoice/FairDivision/Chores.lean` defines additive cost, feasibility-facing lemmas, envy-freeness, EFX, and the empty-bundle convention. `PaperInterface.lean` uses these predicates in every source-facing statement.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: For distinct positive values `p < q`, Lean rescales the additive cost profile by `1/p`, proves EFX is invariant under that positive rescaling, and dispatches the normalized `{1,q/p}` instance by whether `q/p <= 2` or `2 < q/p`.
model_conventions.why_needed: The paper introduces the normalized `(1,r)` presentation after defining general nonnegative bi-valued costs. The public theorem retains the literal general bi-valued quantification; constant-valued and binary `{0,q}` profiles are handled separately rather than being excluded by normalization.
model_conventions.checked_scope: `BiValuedReduction.lean`, `FullBiValuedDispatch.lean`, `ConstantBiValued.lean`, `BinaryChores.lean`, and the rescaling theorems in `Chores.lean` prove this bridge without an additional paper-facing premise.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: For normalized high-ratio instances, an M2 chore is represented by the two-element finite set of agents for whom it is small; multiplicities of these pairs form the source multigraph. M01 and M34 are represented by the corresponding cardinality predicates on the same small-agent set.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source shifts between chore pools and a multigraph. The explicit finite-set representation makes the pool partition, endpoint ownership, graph relabelling, and allocation feasibility checkable in the same model.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Build the displayed finite tri-valued instance and derive the no-EFX contradiction from the large-item and minimum-cost counting propositions; extend it to every n at least four in Appendix A.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For every natural n at least four, Lean constructs a tri-valued additive chore instance with no feasible EFX allocation.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The public endpoint `tri_valued_nonexistence` has exactly `tri_valued_nonexistenceSpec`; the four-agent and Appendix propositions are separately exposed and proved.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Use the two-group `(1,r)` construction, show every EFX bundle has a large item and the stated cost lower bounds, then construct a Pareto improvement for an arbitrary EFX allocation.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For every n at least four and r greater than ceil(n/2)+1, Lean constructs a `(1,r)` instance in which no EFX allocation is Pareto-optimal.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The group sizes, item counts, strict r bound, EFX subpropositions, and the Pareto-improvement conclusion are visible in the public specifications.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Insert an M34 item through the acyclic most-envy graph and obtain the direct cost-gap composition inequalities for a prefix and residue.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Lean proves EFX-preserving M34 insertion and both the unit-slack and general cost-gap composition implications.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The composition API isolates the inequality argument; allocation-of-pool bookkeeping is retained by its callers whenever a source construction is combined.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Construct canonical and super-canonical M01 prefixes, orient M2 multigraph edges, characterize the two exceptional M2 residues, and combine a gap-filled prefix with a selected residue allocation.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Lean proves the named canonical, balanced-orientation, M2-existence, M2-properties, and exceptional-residue-combination lemmas with concrete constructors rather than a supplied allocation certificate.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The M2-property endpoint includes the ordinary small-item slack/large-only envy-free alternatives, the two exceptional shapes, and the preferred endpoint property for complementary pair types.

checked_proof_steps.source_step: Handle low ratios by the source reverse-first-round round robin; for high ratios partition into M01, M2, and M34, close the b modulo four concatenation cases and insert M34 chores; then undo positive normalization and cover equal-value and binary profiles.
checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For every finite four-agent bi-valued additive chore instance, Lean constructs a feasible EFX allocation.
checked_proof_steps.scope: `four_agent_bi_valued_efx_exists` is the exact public source theorem. The high-ratio proof has no remaining outer graph or residue dispatcher boundary.
